S019.name: Delusions
S019.description: Fixed beliefs that do not change easily, even in the face of contradictory evidence.

subtypes.Persecutory Delusions: The false belief that one is being harmed or monitored by other people or organizations.
subtypes.Referential Delusions: The conviction that ordinary events, remarks, or behaviors have specific relevance to oneself.
subtypes.Grandiose Delusions: The false belief that one possesses special abilities, power, or fame.
subtypes.Erotomanic Delusions: The false belief that another person is in love with or has affection for them.
subtypes.Nihilistic Delusions: A destructive or negative conviction that the world is ending or that a major catastrophe will occur.
subtypes.Somatic Delusions: The baseless conviction that there is a serious abnormality with one's body or organs.
subtypes.Jealous Delusions: The conviction that one's spouse or romantic partner is being unfaithful without sufficient evidence.

S020.name: Hallucinations
S020.description: Perception-like experiences that occur without an external stimulus and are as vivid and clear as normal perception.

subtypes.Auditory Hallucinations: The perceptual experience of hearing voices or sounds when there is no actual sound.
subtypes.Visual Hallucinations: The perceptual experience of seeing people or objects that do not exist.
subtypes.Tactile Hallucinations: Experiencing the sensation of being touched or movement on the skin when there is no actual stimulus.
subtypes.Olfactory Hallucinations: The perceptual experience of smelling odors that do not exist.
subtypes.Gustatory Hallucinations: The perceptual experience of tasting flavors that are not actually present.

S022.name: Disorganized_Abnormal_Behavior
S022.description: A state where behavior and motor control are severely disturbed, appearing as movements or reactions inappropriate to the situation.

subtypes.Childlike Silliness: Inappropriate, childish, or illogical behavior appearing in situations.
subtypes.Stupor: No psychomotor activity; not actively relating to environment.
subtypes.Catalepsy: Passive induction of a posture held against gravity.
subtypes.Waxy Flexibility: Slight, even resistance to positioning by examiner.
subtypes.Mutism: No, or very little, verbal response despite the ability to speak.
subtypes.Negativism: Opposition or no response to instructions or external stimuli without apparent motive.
subtypes.Posturing: Spontaneous and active maintenance of a posture against gravity.
subtypes.Mannerism: Odd, circumstantial caricature of normal actions.
subtypes.Agitation: Excessive motor activity without obvious external cause.
subtypes.Grimacing: Contorted facial expressions irrelevant to the situation.

S023.name: Negative_Symptoms
S023.description: A state where emotions, motivation, speech, or social interest that should normally be present are diminished or lost.

subtypes.Diminished Emotional Expression: A state of reduced emotional expression in facial expressions, eye contact, intonation of speech, and movements.
subtypes.Avolition: A decrease in motivated self-initiated purposeful activities.
subtypes.Alogia: A state where the quantity of spontaneous speech is significantly reduced.
subtypes.Anhedonia: A decrease in the ability to experience pleasure or interest in enjoyable activities.
subtypes.Asociality: A state where interest in social activities or interpersonal relationships is significantly reduced.

symptom.disease_info: Schizophrenia is a chronic psychotic disorder characterized by at least six months of disturbance with one or more month of active-phase symptoms such as delusions, hallucinations, disorganized thinking or behavior, and negative symptoms, along with clear functional decline. It typically emerges in late adolescence or early adulthood, with women often presenting somewhat later than men, and follows a variable course with episodes of exacerbation and partial remission. Diagnosis requires that symptoms are not better explained by mood disorders with psychotic features, substance use, or medical conditions, and that the psychotic features are prominent even outside of mood episodes. Stressful life events, substance use, and social adversity can precipitate or worsen episodes, but are not viewed as sole causes; genetic vulnerability and neurodevelopmental factors underlie the illness.

patient.stressor: Kathy had long managed the demands of teaching, coaching, and organizing arts events, but about 14 months ago, during a particularly intense school year with a new standardized curriculum rollout, colleagues began noticing that she was withdrawing from committees and seemed less engaged in her usually dynamic lessons. She started missing deadlines for curriculum planning, cancelling community theater rehearsals, and avoiding social gatherings she once organized, attributing it to "burnout" and midlife health concerns. Over the following year and two months, her classroom presence changed enough that students and parents complained about her flat manner and reduced interaction, and the principal raised concerns during her performance review about a clear decline from her previous high level of functioning. After she quietly requested to step back from coaching and was nearly placed on a performance improvement plan, her spouse and a trusted coworker encouraged her to see a psychiatrist when it became evident that her loss of motivation and reduced participation were far beyond ordinary stress and were jeopardizing her career and community roles.
patient.chief_complaint: “I feel like I’ve lost the drive and interest in everything I used to care about, even my students and the arts stuff I loved.”

S019.name: Delusions
S019.description: Fixed beliefs that do not change easily, even in the face of contradictory evidence.
S019.manifestation: Over this past year I’ve become convinced that the new standardized curriculum isn’t just about test scores, that it was designed to target me specifically and make me look incompetent, even though my husband and coworkers keep telling me that’s irrational and that everyone is dealing with the same changes.

S020.name: Hallucinations
S020.description: Perception-like experiences that occur without an external stimulus and are as vivid and clear as normal perception.
S020.manifestation: Sometimes when I’m in my classroom after school, straightening up or trying to plan, I hear a couple of voices—one male, one female—commenting on my teaching and saying things like, “She’s failing them,” even though I know there’s no one actually in the room with me.

S022.name: Disorganized_Abnormal_Behavior
S022.description: A state where behavior and motor control are severely disturbed, appearing as movements or reactions inappropriate to the situation.
S022.manifestation: My students and colleagues have pointed out, and I’ve noticed it too, that I’ll suddenly stop mid-lesson and just stand there staring at the whiteboard or fiddling with the same stack of papers for several minutes, completely losing track of what I was doing while the class sits there confused until someone speaks up to snap me out of it.

S023.name: Negative_Symptoms
S023.description: A state where emotions, motivation, speech, or social interest that should normally be present are diminished or lost.
S023.manifestation: It’s like the spark I used to have for my students and for directing the community theater just went out—I go through the motions of teaching and come home to sit on the couch, ignoring lesson plans and scripts, because I can’t seem to care enough to start anything even though I know it’s all slipping away from me.

add_requirements.functional_impairment: Over this past school year my teaching evaluations have dropped, I nearly ended up on a performance improvement plan, and I’ve stepped back from coaching and theater because I just can’t manage them anymore, which has strained relationships with colleagues, students, and friends who relied on me.
add_requirements.duration: Looking back, I can see that this loss of drive and the gradual pulling away from my usual school and arts activities has been building for a little over a year now, starting around the time the new curriculum was rolled out.
add_requirements.psychotic_symptoms_duration: The idea that the curriculum is targeting me and the voices criticizing my teaching have only been happening for the last few months, maybe since late in this past semester.
